Instructions

  1. Perform a typical Thunderdome* with one adjustment. When you write out a potential Strengthen correct answer on the Argument stimuli, follow these guidelines:

    1. If the argument is causal, write your own Grouped Opposite.

    2. If the argument contains a Flipper, write your own Flipper correct answer.

    3. If the argument is not causal and doesn't contain a Flipper, write your own Defective Necessary Assumption.

sections.html:
Ellen's Advice

If You Want to Win

  • It is not important to look at the question stem and answer choices during a Thunderdome.

    • The point of this workout is not to answer questions, but if you want to combine it with answer-choosing, I'm not fully against it.

  • Don't attempt to Thunderdome as a beginner.

    • If you haven't met the Translation time goal or don't have significant experience with full LR sections, wait to Thunderdome until you need it.

  • For the right kind of plateaued, advanced test taker, Thunderdomes offer a singular opportunity for a perspective shift.

  • Thunderdomes show you where you're weak.

    • If you find that you always struggle with one of the Thunderdome outputs, review the videos and written material on that topic.

  • Thunderdomes are great for when you start to run out of unseen PTs near the end of your prep.

    • Thunderdomes can still be done on previously seen material.

  • If you are an advanced student PTing at 172+, Thunderdoming can take your skills to the next level.

  • Like Translation + CLIR Drills, Thunderdomes are a great spot to use AI voice dictation to speed up the workout. My favorite dictation software is Flow; it's free up to 2000 words per week.
